Buy Properties at a Fraction of Their Value at Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania Tax Deed Sale

Get properties up to 90% below market value at the Schuylkill County Pennsylvania tax sales! Hosted at the Majestic Theatre in Pottsville, these auctions offer various sale types, including Upset, Private, Judicial, and Repository sales, each designed to facilitate your entry into property investment.

Schuylkill County Tax Sale Types:

  1. Upset Sale:
    • Date: Held in September.
    • Details: Schuylkill County sells properties with existing liens and encumbrances. It publishes listings 30 days before the sale in local newspapers and on its website.
    • Bid Procedure: The highest bidder wins.
  2. Private Sale:
    • Eligibility: This offer is available for properties not sold at the Upset Sale. It is open only to those without delinquent taxes or outstanding municipal bills in Pennsylvania.
    • Details: Properties are sold as-is with all liens and encumbrances. The process may take 6-12 months.
  3. Judicial Sale:
    • Details: Schuylkill County judicial sale offers properties free of most encumbrances but without title guarantees. It requires preparation, including title searches and court petitions.
    • Frequency: Held irregularly, aiming for at least two per year.
  4. Repository Sale:
    • Details: For properties unsold at the Judicial Sale, available anytime upon receiving a bid. The minimum bid generally matches the Judicial Sale cost.
    • Unique Feature: Offers a unique chance to bid with fewer competitors.

Pro Tips in Investing at Schuylkill County Tax Sale:

  • Do Your Homework: Always conduct a thorough title search and due diligence before bidding.
  • Check Regulations: Understand the local laws and regulations governing tax sales in Schuylkill County.
  • Prepare for Delays: Be aware that the private sale process can be lengthy, often taking 6-12 months.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

  1. What is a Tax Lien Certificate?
  • The county issues a tax lien certificate when property owners fail to pay their taxes. Investors can purchase these certificates, which offer the right to collect unpaid taxes plus interest from the property owner.
  1. How often are tax sales held in Schuylkill County?
  • The Upset Sale is held annually in September. Judicial Sales are irregular but aim for at least two per year.
  1. Can anyone participate in the tax sales?
  • Yes, but for Private Sales, bidders must not have any delinquent taxes or outstanding municipal bills in Pennsylvania.
  1. What happens if I purchase a property at a Judicial Sale?
  • The county sells properties with existing liens and encumbrances. It publishes listings 30 days before the sale in local newspapers and on its website.
